Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks for the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the logging / PII requirements we covered: 

Summary from the call:
- FintechCo needs request/response logs for troubleshooting and audit, but with strong redaction controls for PII (SSNs, account numbers, email addresses, payment tokens).
- Headers to consider: Authorization tokens should never be stored in plaintext; Cookie and Set-Cookie should be stripped. Trace IDs are useful for debugging but need to be hashed/pseudonymized to maintain traceability without exposing raw IDs.
- Retention ask: FintechCo prefers raw traceable data retention no longer than 30 days; aggregated metrics and observability data can be kept longer.

Proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm the top fields you want redacted (we captured ssn, account_number, email, payment_token, user_ip) and whether you prefer hashing vs full redact?
2) We'll follow up with a proposed redaction mapping (per-field) and a short technical note on how trace IDs and headers are handled.

I'll loop in Dev and Rishi for the technical detail. If you can reply with a sample (redacted) log snippet or confirm fields, we'll get the mapping to you within 48 business hours.

Hi Alex / Priya — great notes, thanks. Technical response and proposal below.

What Redwood can do now (summary):
1) Field-level redaction: we support schema-driven redaction (JSON path) + regex-based rules. Options per-field: 
   - FULL_REDACT: replace with "[REDACTED]"
   - HASH_DET:<salted-hmac> : deterministic HMAC with customer salt (useful for trace correlation across services)
   - TOKENIZE: KMS-backed reversible tokenization (requires separate contract / private deploy option)

2) Headers: Authorization header will be hashed (HASH_DET) if requested; we can also strip Authorization and only retain request metadata. Cookie/Set-Cookie will be stripped by default. X-Forwarded-For / user_ip can be stored as /24 masked, or stored as deterministic hash depending on compliance need.

3) Trace IDs: we recommend deterministic HMAC hashing with a customer-scoped salt (so FintechCo can correlate across systems that use the same salt). This preserves the ability to join traces without keeping raw values. We store both the hashed value and a small per-request metadata blob (no raw IDs).

4) Retention enforcement: automated purge jobs enforce retention windows at the storage layer. For hosted customers we provide a retention policy UI and API to set 30d/90d/365d; for Dedicated/Private deployments you can set custom policies and retain full audit logs locally.

Attachments: attaching a proposed redaction mapping (.csv) and a short technical brief (redwood-logging-redaction-overview.pdf). Also including a redacted copy of our SOC2 summary for your security team (SOC2_report_redacted.pdf).

Next steps we need from FintechCo:
- Confirm per-field action (FULL_REDACT vs HASH_DET vs TOKENIZE) for: ssn, account_number, payment_token, card_pan, email, phone_number, user_ip, trace_id.
- Confirm retention windows for raw logs vs pseudonymized logs.
- If you want deterministic hashing across systems, provide guidance on salt management (we can manage per-customer salt in KMS or you're welcome to provide).

If it helps, I'm happy to demo the redaction UI in a follow-up call. Proposed availability: Wed Jun 3 10am PT or Thu Jun 4 9am PT.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
